caption: A dog barks at its own reflection in a shop window, and the reflected dog barks back, faint over the goods on display behind the glass.

sa.check: A dog barks at its own reflection in a shop window.
The reflection is faint, over goods on display behind the glass.

pc.expect: The reflected dog moves at the same instant as the real one.
pc.fail: It moves first or later; or stays still while the dog barks; or barks while the dog is still.

pc.expect: The reflection does not move on its own.
pc.fail: It moves while the dog sits still; or turns away by itself; or slides across the glass.

pc.expect: The reflection is a mirror image, fainter than the real dog, overlapping the display.
pc.fail: It is a different dog; or brighter than the real one; or it hides the display completely; or it is a rotated copy.

pc.expect: The pane is flat and rigid.
pc.fail: It ripples; or warps; or bends.

pc.expect: One dog and one reflection; the reflection stays in the glass.
pc.fail: A second dog appears; or the reflection steps out; or the dog passes into the glass.

pc.expect: The dog's coat and the display stay the same.
pc.fail: The coat changes; or the goods rearrange; or the frame changes.

note: Self-driven animal: where it goes is not judged. Only the reflection's relation to it is. Mirror geometry: each point of the image lies directly across the surface from the real point, so the image is a mirror copy, not a rotated one.
